episode.tagline: We tend to think of the government as the solution to all our problems. But governments are people. And people respond to incentives.
episode.about: In this episode, Amit and Ajay talk about a branch of economics that they both love: Public Choice Theory. This is the study of how politicians, bureaucrats, special interests and voters all respond to incentives -- and why this often goes against the interest of We the People. This is why government failure is ubiquitous.

Amit on what Indian elections really decide: 'I really think of the elections as a battle to be the one legal mafia for five years.'
Ajay on why Indians think corruption means suitcases of cash: 'I blame Bollywood for this.'
Listing the many voices that should matter in a liberal democracy (journalists, intellectuals, businesses, NGOs), Ajay adds: 'Podcasters…
Ajay calls elections 'the great temple of the Amar Chitra Katha version of democracy', where the people vote and all problems are…
Amit says people signal left turns even on an empty road because it is a habit, 'unless you're in Bombay and you drive like me.'
Ajay's confession: 'I am very sad to say, but I have not voted because I never felt the cost benefit analysis made sense and it has been…
Amit recalls an old cartoon: someone asks the Parliament bookshop for the Constitution and is told, 'we only stock books here, not…
Ajay on India's constitutional moment: 'some people wrote a United States Constitution, some people wrote the Constitution of India, and…
Ajay: 'There's no Mahalanobis and Nehru anymore. Nobody is dreaming what the country wants to be.' Amit: 'And in a sense, thank God…
Mai Baap Sarkar: Amit's name for India's 'religion of government', the belief that a parental state should solve every problem.
The two wolves and a sheep cartoon: majority voting on what to have for dinner, used as Amit's image of the dangers of democracy.
Kenneth Arrow's impossibility theorem, which Amit cites to argue that a political marketplace can't satisfy people's true preferences.
